01

What we show

Built and verified live
  • Custom matching engine + review workspace, native in Salesforce. Real emails and real texts matched to the right booking, with plain-language reasons on screen for every decision.
  • Four cases, one at a time: one open booking auto-files on identity alone. Two open bookings auto-files when the message content (event date + booking-name words) singles one out. Genuinely ambiguous waits in a review queue with ranked candidates. Bare "thank you" / "ok" replies are filtered before matching runs.
  • Texts work identically (phone number instead of address), and every rule (strictness, junk phrases, content checks) is org-editable.

What he will see on screen

The review queue. One message waiting, with ranked booking candidates and the reasons for each on the right.

Content match with two open bookings. The message named the gala and its date, so it auto-filed to the gala booking. Both reasons are spelled out, and the runner-up shows why it lost.

The ambiguous case waits for a person. Identity alone cannot pick between two bookings, so a reviewer confirms with one click. The footnote under the candidates is the live competitor comparison for this exact message.

Texts, same engine. A real inbound text matched from the phone number to the client booking.

The junk filter. A bare "Ok" text and a "thank you" email landed in the collapsible Filtered section, out of the queue but never lost.

Tunable rules. Match strictness, the junk phrase list, and the content safeguard are org settings, changed here, effective immediately.

02

Why we win

Verified on live docs 8/12
Them (their own docs)Us
Match My Email matches on header email addresses. Its precision path is a "Name Tag": a tag word planted in the subject line by a templated OUTBOUND email, so precise matching only works when the client replies inside that thread. A brand new inbound message has no tag and falls back to address matching, which their own docs admit causes multi-opportunity "clutter". Custom rules are gated behind their support staff, there is no native SMS (they refer you to a partner product), and it runs $11 to $12 per user per month, forever.Reads the message itself: event name, date, event type. No tags, no codes, no reply-thread dependency. The logic lives in WTA's own org, so every rule is theirs to tune, and there is no per-user fee.
Einstein Activity Capture picks ONE record by tiebreakers (close date, owner, last-modified) without reading the message. Salesforce's own docs warn it "can match an older or recently closed opportunity." Retention limits apply. No SMS.Auto-files only clear winners, everything else waits for a person. Records are permanent ordinary Salesforce data. SMS through the same engine.
Both are vendor black boxes.Client-owned code in their org, tunable to their rules.
